record.paper_title: Statements and open problems on decidable sets X ⊆ N that contain informal notions and refer to the current knowledge on X
record.original_question: Are there infinitely many primes of the form k! + 1, where k! denotes the factorial of the positive integer k?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2.1. ([1, p. 443], [5]). The are infinitely many primes of the form k! + 1.

artifact.self_contained_problem: For a positive integer $k$, let $k! = 1 \cdot 2 \cdot 3 \cdots k$ denote the factorial of $k$. A prime of the form $k!+1$ is called a factorial prime (of the "+1" type). Determine whether there exist infinitely many positive integers $k$ such that $k!+1$ is prime.
artifact.status_search_result: The infinitude of primes of the form k!+1 is a long-standing open conjecture in number theory. Only finitely many such primes are currently known (with values of k tabulated in OEIS A002981), and no proof of infinitude is known.

status_evidence.title: Factorial prime - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: It is conjectured that there are infinitely many factorial primes, but this has not been proven.
status_evidence.claim: Infinitude of factorial primes is conjectured but unproven.

status_evidence.title: OEIS A002981
status_evidence.snippet: Numbers k such that k! + 1 is prime.
status_evidence.claim: Only a finite list of known k with k!+1 prime is recorded; infinitude is open.
